newsitem.title: USA: Deceased woman's family hires Kevorkian attorney.
newsitem.headline: Deceased woman's family hires Kevorkian attorney.

text.p: One day after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down doctor-assisted suicide, the lawyer for Dr. Jack Kevorkian said he had been retained to represent the family of a Nevada woman whose body was found on Friday morning in a Michigan motel room.

Attorney Geoffrey Fieger said Janice Murphy of Henderson, Nevada, who suffered from chronic fatigue syndrome, was brought to Michigan by her father. Fieger refused to say whether Kevorkian was involved in the death.

Murphy's death fits the pattern of several others this year in the Detroit area that authorities suspect were suicides assisted by the 69-year-old retired pathologist. Kevorkian has admitted being present at 45 deaths since 1990 as part of his crusade to legalise physician-assisted suicide, but authorities suspect the actual number is higher.

Southfield Police Lt. Steven Lasota, who gave Murphy's age as 40, said the Oakland County Medical Examiner's office got an anonymous call notifying them of a body at the Residence Inn. A note on the body instructed authorities to call Fieger.
"At this point, let's just say it's a suspicious death," Lasota said.
County Medical Examiner Ljubisa Dragovic, who was performing an autopsy on Murphy's body on Friday, has declared earlier deaths associated with Kevorkian to be homicides.
Fieger on Thursday lambasted the Supreme Court's ruling that Americans do not have a constitutional right to physician- assisted suicide.

A judge in Ionia County, Michigan, this month declared a mistrial in the fourth Kevorkian assisted-suicide trial. Prosecutor Raymond Voet has not said whether he will bring new charges against Kevorkian, who was acquitted at three earlier trials involving five deaths.
